sources.author_or_institution: Rudolf Haag, Jan T. Lopuszanski, and Martin Sohnius; CERN Document Server
sources.title: All Possible Generators of Supersymmetries of the S-Matrix
sources.adaptation_notes: The classification argument and graded-algebra constraints were recast as self-contained matrix, sign, Lorentz-spin, and three-dimensional central-charge exercises. Wording and derivations are original to this edition.

sources.author_or_institution: Philip C. Argyres, University of Cincinnati
sources.title: An Introduction to Global Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: General discussions of the super-Poincare algebra, particle representations, positivity, and R symmetry were reorganized into proofs using the notation and normalizations of Chapter 25. No source solutions were reproduced.

sources.author_or_institution: Adel Bilal, University of Neuchatel
sources.title: Introduction to Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The algebra, representation, extended-supersymmetry, and BPS themes were separated into new derivational exercises on central charges, massive multiplets, shortening, and parity. Solutions were independently derived in local conventions.

sources.author_or_institution: David Tong, University of Cambridge
sources.title: Supersymmetric Field Theory
sources.adaptation_notes: Graduate-lecture material on algebra representations, CPT completion, extended multiplets, and BPS bounds was converted into chapter-specific counting and proof problems. Prompts, notation, and all worked solutions were independently written.

sources.author_or_institution: Stephen P. Martin, Northern Illinois University
sources.title: A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.adaptation_notes: The introductory particle-content discussion was used only as a provenance anchor for new helicity-construction exercises on chiral and vector multiplets. The local prompts and solutions were not copied from the notes.

sources.author_or_institution: Philip C. Argyres; University of Cincinnati
sources.title: An Introduction to Global Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The official four-component graduate notes were used as a provenance anchor for new exercises on general and chiral superfields, Kahler transformations, moduli, discrete transformations, and improved currents. Every prompt and derivation was rewritten in the conventional four-component notation of Volume III.

sources.author_or_institution: Adel Bilal, University of Neuchatel
sources.title: Introduction to Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: Public graduate-lecture discussions of superspace, chiral actions, F-term breaking, the goldstino, and nonlinear sigma models were separated into new component and proof exercises. Solutions were independently derived and translated into the chapter's Majorana conventions.

sources.author_or_institution: David Tong, University of Cambridge
sources.title: Supersymmetric Field Theory
sources.adaptation_notes: The official Part III lecture material on chiral superfields, F- and D-terms, Wess-Zumino models, nonlinear sigma models, and O'Raifeartaigh breaking informed new chapter-specific calculations. No source problem or solution text was reproduced.

sources.author_or_institution: Stephen P. Martin, Northern Illinois University
sources.title: A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.adaptation_notes: The verified version-7 sections on chiral Lagrangians, superspace, nonrenormalizable operators, and supersymmetry breaking were used to design independent dimensional-analysis and component exercises. All notation was converted to Volume III's conventional four-component formalism.

sources.author_or_institution: Philip C. Argyres; University of Cincinnati
sources.title: An Introduction to Global Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The author's official four-component graduate notes were used as a provenance anchor for new exercises on vector superfields, Wess-Zumino gauge, Abelian and non-Abelian field strengths, Fayet-Iliopoulos terms, Higgsing, and Coulomb-branch surface charges. Prompts and complete solutions were independently written in Volume III conventions.

sources.author_or_institution: Adel Bilal, University of Neuchatel
sources.title: Introduction to Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: Public graduate lectures on supersymmetric gauge actions, spontaneous and soft breaking, holomorphy, N=2 Yang-Mills theory, Coulomb branches, and BPS states informed new chapter-specific derivations. All prompts were adapted and credited; all solutions were independently derived in conventional four-component notation.

sources.author_or_institution: David Tong, University of Cambridge
sources.title: Supersymmetric Field Theory
sources.adaptation_notes: The author's official Part III material on non-renormalization, supersymmetry breaking, supersymmetric QED and Yang-Mills theory, vacuum moduli spaces, and extended supersymmetry was reorganized into new exercises tightly matched to Chapter 27. No prompt or solution text was reproduced.

sources.author_or_institution: Stephen P. Martin, Northern Illinois University
sources.title: A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.adaptation_notes: The verified public primer was used as a provenance anchor for independently designed component exercises on gauge actions, auxiliary fields, Fayet-Iliopoulos breaking, goldstino mixing, supertraces, and soft terms. Notation and derivations were converted throughout to the four-component conventions of Volume III.

sources.author_or_institution: Stephen P. Martin, Northern Illinois University
sources.title: A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.adaptation_notes: The author's verified version-7 primer informed eight new exercises on matter parity, unification thresholds, gauge-mediated gaugino ratios, radiative electroweak breaking, neutralinos, sfermion mixing, and LSP stability. Prompts and worked solutions were independently written in Volume III's conventional four-component notation.

sources.author_or_institution: Manuel Drees; Asia-Pacific Center for Theoretical Physics and KEK
sources.title: An Introduction to Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The public graduate lectures on the MSSM field content, electroweak symmetry breaking, Higgs masses and mixing, radiative corrections, and chargino mixing were reorganized into eight chapter-specific derivations. All wording and complete solutions are original to this exercise edition.

sources.author_or_institution: G. F. Giudice and R. Rattazzi; CERN
sources.title: Theories with Gauge-Mediated Supersymmetry Breaking
sources.adaptation_notes: The verified CERN review supplied provenance for seven independent exercises on messenger spectra, holomorphic gaugino thresholds, scalar Casimirs, unified messenger indices, flavor universality, the gravitino LSP, and the mu-Bmu problem. No source exercise or solution text was copied.

sources.author_or_institution: D. J. H. Chung, L. L. Everett, G. L. Kane, S. F. King, J. Lykken, and Lian-Tao Wang
sources.title: The Soft Supersymmetry-Breaking Lagrangian: Theory and Applications
sources.adaptation_notes: The public review's treatments of soft flavor tensors, mass insertions, lepton-flavor violation, physical CP phases, dipole moments, and R-parity violation informed seven new exercises. Prompts and derivations were independently composed and matched to Chapter 28 notation.

sources.author_or_institution: David Tong, University of Cambridge
sources.title: Supersymmetric Field Theory and Example Sheets 2-4
sources.locator: Chapter 3, Section 3.4; Example Sheet 2, Questions 1 and 3; Example Sheet 3, Questions 1, 4, and 5; Example Sheet 4, Question 1
sources.adaptation_notes: The official Cambridge Part III notes and dated 2023 example sheets were used to design eight new problems on the Witten index, goldstino direction, spurion holomorphy, one-loop running, instanton weights, ADS vacua, and Abelian field-strength components. Prompts and four-component solutions were independently written.

sources.author_or_institution: Adel Bilal, University of Neuchatel
sources.title: Introduction to Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The author-posted graduate lectures on the exact low-energy N=2 action, Abelian dualization, the integral duality group, dyon charges, BPS masses, singularities, and Seiberg-Witten monodromies informed eight independently composed derivations translated into Volume III conventions.

sources.author_or_institution: Kenneth Intriligator and Nathan Seiberg
sources.title: Lectures on Supersymmetric Gauge Theories and Electric-Magnetic Duality
sources.adaptation_notes: The public author-posted review supplied provenance for seven new exercises on Wilsonian holomorphy, anomaly-free R charges, the ADS superpotential, holomorphic decoupling, gaugino condensation, quantum-modified constraints, and orthogonal-group dynamics. All prompts and solutions were independently written.

sources.author_or_institution: Erich Poppitz and Sandip P. Trivedi
sources.title: Dynamical Supersymmetry Breaking
sources.adaptation_notes: The verified public review's treatments of vacuum criteria, runaways, O'Raifeartaigh pseudomoduli, radiative lifting, R-symmetry counting, the 3-2 model, and quantum-constraint rank conditions were reorganized into seven chapter-specific exercises with original solutions.

sources.author_or_institution: S. J. Gates Jr., M. T. Grisaru, M. Rocek, and W. Siegel
sources.title: Superspace, or One Thousand and One Lessons in Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The author-released book's treatment of superspace gauge fixing, chiral and vector propagators, supergraph rules, D-algebra, divergence counting, and sample loop calculations informed twelve independently written exercises. All notation and normalizations were converted to Volume III's four-component conventions.

sources.author_or_institution: Stefan Antusch and Michael Ratz; Technical University of Munich
sources.title: Supergraph Techniques and Two-Loop Beta-Functions for Renormalizable and Non-Renormalizable Operators
sources.adaptation_notes: The author-posted article's wavefunction-renormalization method, tensor beta functions, group factors, and effective-operator examples were reorganized into nine self-contained supergraph and renormalization exercises. Solutions were derived independently in the conventions of Chapter 30.

sources.author_or_institution: Sergei M. Kuzenko and Simon J. Tyler; University of Western Australia
sources.title: The One-Loop Effective Potential of the Wess-Zumino Model Revisited
sources.adaptation_notes: The verified author-posted analysis of chiral projectors, the background-field Hessian, functional determinants, the Kahler approximation, and higher-superderivative terms supplied provenance for nine independently designed exercises. The prompts avoid reproducing the paper's calculations verbatim and use Weinberg's four-component superspace notation.

sources.author_or_institution: Daniel Z. Freedman and Antoine Van Proeyen
sources.title: Ingredients of Supergravity
sources.adaptation_notes: The authors' public lecture summary of their supergravity text supplied provenance for six independently written exercises on vierbeins, spinor curvature, the Rarita-Schwinger gauge symmetry, gravitino degrees of freedom, and the super-Higgs mechanism. All derivations use the four-component conventions and normalizations of Chapter 31.

sources.author_or_institution: Antoine Van Proeyen, KU Leuven
sources.title: Tools for Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The author's public graduate lectures on gauge geometry, gravity, spinors, and anti-de Sitter superalgebras informed six original exercises on torsion, the one-and-a-half-order formalism, local-algebra closure, off-shell balance, supersymmetric AdS vacua, and no-scale cancellation.

sources.author_or_institution: Gian F. Giudice, Markus A. Luty, Hitoshi Murayama, and Riccardo Rattazzi
sources.title: Gaugino Mass without Singlets
sources.adaptation_notes: The author-posted primary article's derivation of superconformal-anomaly soft terms supplied provenance for six independently designed exercises on gaugino masses, trilinears, scalar masses, supersymmetric thresholds, ultraviolet insensitivity, and the slepton-sign problem. No source problem or solution text was reproduced.

sources.author_or_institution: A. Brignole, L. E. Ibanez, and C. Munoz
sources.title: Soft Supersymmetry-Breaking Terms from Supergravity and Superstring Models
sources.adaptation_notes: The verified author-posted review of general N=1 supergravity soft terms informed six independently written exercises on Kahler transformations, Minkowski tuning, gauge-kinetic masses, scalar Kähler curvature, trilinear terms, and flavor universality. The notation was translated throughout to Weinberg's modified Kahler potential and four-component fields.

sources.author_or_institution: Stephen P. Martin, Northern Illinois University
sources.title: A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.adaptation_notes: The author's public pedagogical treatment of supersymmetry breaking, gravitinos, and mediation supplied provenance for six new exercises on Planck suppression, the goldstino direction, longitudinal-gravitino equivalence, decay scaling, Polonyi stability, and hidden-sector scales. Prompts and worked solutions were independently composed for Chapter 31.
